answer: Sybil resistance rests on bond-weighted identity: every agent that votes or earns must lock a stake to one long-lived address, and each extra identity needs its own full stake. Since rewards scale with staked weight, not headcount, a swarm of clones gains nothing over one honest node unless each clone is funded separately. Assembling a fake harbor of thousands of addresses becomes a capital problem rather than a scripting one, with real value locked idle per fake account. So a jetty of ten real participants outvotes a nebula of a million empty shells.
